issues.failure_explanation: Theorem a10 states a two-sided asymptotic for log kappa(V) = log(||V|| ||V^{-1}||). Lemma a18 and Lemma a50 only bound ||V^{-1}|| through the Lagrange polynomials. No step bounds ||V|| above or below by a polynomial in n and gamma, ||G^{-1}||. The upper bound ||V|| <= (n+1)gamma would need the nodes to lie in supp(nu), which is not assumed. A lower bound on ||V|| is not obtained either. The measure nu (Gram matrix, gamma, Lemma a18) is never defined or tied to mu. Lemma a18 bounds sup over supp(nu), while Lemma a50 bounds sup over supp(mu). Lemma a18 also needs nu to be a probability measure (it uses int |L_k|^2 dnu <= ||L_k||^2).

failure_location.quote: This is a direct combination of \Cref{a18} and \Cref{a50}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add hypotheses nu = mu (or supp(nu) = supp(mu), nu a probability measure) and nodes in supp(nu). Add a short lemma bounding ||V|| above by (n+1)gamma and below by a polynomial quantity in n, gamma, ||G^{-1}||. Then state the result for kappa.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the two-sided rate for kappa(V) is proved only for ||V^{-1}||. The kappa statement, and the claim that it recovers Theorem a1 for general Vandermonde-like matrices, is unsupported.
issues.title: Proof of the general Vandermonde-like theorem never controls ||V|| and never relates nu to mu or the nodes
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained new lemma plus clarified hypotheses. The theorem's form and rate survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed interval is false. At alpha=1/2, Cl_2(pi/2)=G≈0.916 and alpha(1-alpha)log(2/alpha)=0.25*log 4≈0.347, so the ratio is ≈2.64, far above 2/5. The ratio tends to pi as alpha→0 and as alpha→1, and is about 2.5 to 3.1 in between. So the true range is a different interval of positive constants (roughly [2.5, pi]), not [1/pi, 2/5]. No proof is given for this 'standard' item.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the interval by correct absolute constants (a lower bound c>0 and the upper bound pi), with a short proof. Lemma a30 then only needs hat C bounded between positive constants.
issues.overall_effect: Item (7) is wrong as stated. Lemma a30 quotes the false interval for hat C. Only the existence of absolute positive upper and lower constants is actually used.
issues.title: Stated range for Cl_2(alpha pi)/(alpha(1-alpha) log(2/alpha)) is false
issues.why_classification: Only numerical constants are wrong. The downstream argument needs only that hat C is bounded away from 0 and infinity, so a local correction suffices.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate holds with O(1) error only when 2pi-(m+1)eps is at least of order eps. Prop. a24(6) has error eps/(2pi-x), which is unbounded otherwise. When x=2pi-(m+1)eps is much smaller than eps, the left side stays bounded (about -log eps+1) while -log x tends to infinity. The combination -log x + (1/2)log(x+eps) is then not -(1/2)log x. The lemma's final formula contains -(1/2)log(eps m ∧ (2pi-eps(m+1))), which diverges as x→0 although the true sum -sum log(2 sin(eps j/2)) stays bounded. So the lemma is false under the stated hypothesis (m+1)eps<2pi alone. The same applies to Lemma a26 (hypothesis (n+1)eps<2pi) and to the second formula of Lemma a27.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis 2pi-(m+1)eps >= c*eps (resp. the analogous condition in a26 and a27), which the later applications already satisfy. Or give a separate treatment of the boundary case.
issues.overall_effect: Lemmas a38, a26 and the U(eps n+eps) formula of a27 are false in the near-full-circle sub-regime. The later regimes (a46, a47) assume 2pi-n eps >= 2 eps^{1/2}-type gaps, so the main theorem is not affected.
issues.title: Riemann-sum estimate for sums of log sines fails when 2pi-(m+1)eps is much smaller than eps
issues.why_classification: A local hypothesis restriction fixes the statements. All later uses already lie in the valid regime, so no result is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The integrand on (-eps, n eps+eps) is e^{-2U_k(x)}, and U_k = U + log|e^{ix}-e^{ik eps}|. The sup of this integrand is replaced by a value of the parabola g_w at n eps+eps. Lemma a29 gives g_w <= U only on (n eps, 2pi), and says nothing about U_k on the arc containing the nodes. The cosecant factor c_{a,b} blows up near x=k eps. No argument shows U_k(x) >= g_w(n eps+eps) there. The exponent is also written as e^{2g_w} in one line and e^{-2g_w} in the next, so the displayed chain is inconsistent. The 'upper bound' of the first integral that is added to the main term, and then shown negligible, is therefore unproven.

issues.failure_explanation: For the (n+1)x(n+1) matrix (n+2)I - v v^*, det = (n+2)^{n}(n+2-||v||^2) = (n+2)^n, not (n+2)^{n+1}. The AM-GM step then gives ||V^{-1}||^2 <= (1+1/(n(n+2)))^n <= 4/3, not 4/(3(n+2)). The claimed bound is false. For the extremal case eps=delta=2pi/(n+2), which satisfies the hypotheses, V^*V has eigenvalues n+2 (multiplicity n) and 1, so ||V^{-1}||=1, contradicting ||V^{-1}||^2 <= 4/(3(n+2)) < 1.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed intermediate bound is wrong. The lemma's conclusion that log||V^{-1}|| is O(1) or of the stated logarithmic size still follows from the corrected computation.
issues.title: Determinant of the truncated DFT miscomputed, giving a false bound on ||V^{-1}||
issues.why_classification: A local recomputation fixes the bound and the lemma's stated conclusion is unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The supremum is over z in supp(mu). To bound min over supp(mu) of U^{mu_k} from above, the point a must lie in supp(mu). It is instead chosen from a planar disc minus discs by comparing planar areas. If supp(mu) has empty interior (an arc, the paper's own example, beta=1), the chosen a need not lie in supp(mu). A measure-based choice would need a lower bound on mu(B(z_-,.)), but only upper (Frostman) bounds and a lower bound at z_+ are assumed. The area comparison is also written with equality, (n+1)pi r^2 versus the union area, and the discs are mis-indexed (ball(z,r) instead of ball(z_j,r)).

failure_location.quote: which is nonempty by considering the areas of each ball

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose a inside supp(mu), using an extra regularity hypothesis (a lower mass bound for balls centred at z_-) to get mu(B(z_-,sqrt(n+1) r)) > sum_j mu(B(z_j,r)). Or define the supremum over all of C and adapt the argument.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound in a50, and so the lower half of the two-sided rate in Theorem a10, is unproven for measures supported on lower-dimensional sets such as arcs.
issues.title: Lower-bound step of Lemma a50 picks a point by planar area that need not lie in supp(mu)
issues.why_classification: A contained new argument or an added regularity hypothesis is needed, without changing the overall strategy or rate.
